items.t: Elon Musk’s growing SpaceX empire sends AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile shares plunging
items.d: Elon Musk’s plan for SpaceX to become a major mobile carrier sent shares of AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile plunging and wiped out over $50 billion before lunch.
items.fullText: Corporations Elon Musk’s growing SpaceX empire sends AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile shares plunging The company announced plans to “become a major mobile carrier in the U.S.” in part by buying spectrum and deploying satellites for its Starlink service. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Starlink's mobile internet business is the single biggest money maker for Elon Musk's flagship company, SpaceX. Finn Gomez / Getty Share Add NBC News to Google Oct. 9, 2026, 1:55 PM EDT / Updated Oct. 9, 2026, 4:26 PM EDT By Steve Kopack Elon Musk’s plan for SpaceX to “become a major mobile carrier in the U.S.” sent shares of the nation’s big three wireless carriers sliding by double digits Friday, wiping out more than $50 billion in market value before lunch. “Once we receive final FCC approval, Starlink Mobile will deploy a flexible architecture combining our satellite-to-mobile constellation in space with an advanced terrestrial deployment that can seamlessly connect devices everywhere,” the company said late Thursday. It also announced that the Federal Communications Commission had approved the launch of 15,000 new satellites, also under Starlink Mobile, which is a subsidiary of SpaceX. Shares of AT&T fell 9.8%, Verizon dropped 8.7%, while T-Mobile US plunged 13.3%. For Verizon, today’s performance was its worst-one day drop since 2002. It was T-Mobile’s worst day since 2011. Shares of Charter and of Comcast, the parent company of NBC News, also fell Friday. Both companies sell wireless services under their own brands using Verizon’s infrastructure. Musk’s empire expands The announcement from SpaceX marked Musk’s latest step to expand his global tech empire. The world’s richest man and its first-ever trillionaire , Musk’s net worth as of Thursday was about $990 billion. items.t: 스페이스X 목표가 254달러…월가 AI·우주 주목 [월가 업&다운]
items.fullText: 핫픽! 미국주식 핫픽! 미국주식 스페이스X 목표가 254달러…월가 AI·우주 주목 [월가 업&다운] 입력 2026.10.09 22:02 수정 2026.10.09 22:45 기사 스크랩 기사 스크랩 댓글 댓글 기사 공유 공유 글자크기 조절 글자크기 프린트 프린트 황정수 기자 구독하기 구글 검색 선호 출처로 추가 Google 검색에서 한국경제 기사를 더 자주 볼 수 있습니다. AI 기사요약 미국 증권사들이 엔비디아와 테슬라 등 주요 기술성장주뿐만 아니라 금융, 헬스케어, 철강 등 다양한 산업군에 대해 일제히 긍정적인 투자 의견을 제시하며 매수세를 확대하고 있습니다. 엔비디아 AI 수요 견조 아멕스·휴매나·CBOE도 상향 애플은 AI 대응 과제 부각 철강·바이오·외식주에도 매수 의견 사진=로이터 연합뉴스 미국 증권사가 9일(현지 시간) 엔비디아(Nvidia)와 테슬라(Tesla), 스페이스X(SpaceX)를 비롯한 성장주에 잇따라 긍정적인 의견을 내놨다. AI와 우주·항공산업의 성장 기대가 이어지는 가운데 금융·헬스케어·철강 등으로도 매수 의견이 확산하는 모습이다. 피지컬AI에 투자하려면 테슬라 CNBC에 따르면 UBS는 엔비디아에 ‘매수’를 유지했다. 9월 대만 수출지표의 절대 규모가 높은 수준을 이어가고 있다는 점을 근거로 AI 수요가 여전히 견조하다고 평가했다. AI 가속기 투자와 서버 구축이 이어지는 상황에서 엔비디아의 수요 기반이 크게 약화하지 않았다는 판단이다. 요크빌 아이브스(Yorkville Ives)는 테슬라에 ‘시장수익률 상회’로 신규 커버리지를 시작했다. 상장시장에서 이른바 ‘피지컬 AI’에 투자할 수 있는 가장 명확한 종목 가운데 하나라고 평가하면서 테슬라의 성장 스토리가 아직 초기 단계에 있다고 봤다. 자동차 판매 자체보다는 로봇과 자율주행 등 장기 사업 가치에 무게를 둔 평가다. 한경 프리미엄9의 모든 콘텐츠는 한국경제신문의 저작물로 저작권법의 보호를 받습니다. 사전 허가 없는 무단 전재·복제·배포·캡처 공유·AI 학습 활용 및 상업적 이용을 금합니다. 위반 시 서비스 이용 제한 및 민형사상 법적 책임이 발생할 수 있습니다. 무료 열람 혜택으로 기사를 읽으셨습니다. 한경 프리미엄9을 구독하고 무제한으로 만나보세요. 구독하기 AI 뉴스 Q&A 더 궁금한 점이 있으신가요? 읽으면서 머릿속에 맴돌던 질문들, 앨리스가 대답해 드릴게요. 인공지능(AI)을 활용해 생성되었으며, 일부 내용에 오류가 있을 수 있습니다. AI 포인트 뷰 이전 분석 종목 다음 분석 종목 본 서비스의 AI가 제공하는 종목 정보는 정보 제공 목적의 참고 자료일 뿐, 투자 권유·자문·추천에 해당하지 않습니다. 투자에 따른 손실 책임은 사용자에게 있습니다. 좋아요 싫어요 후속기사 원해요 황정수 특파원 안녕하세요. 국제부 뉴욕특파원입니다. 기사댓글 개의 댓글이 있습니다. 댓글 닫기

items.t: Xona’s commercial GPS alternative is about to go live
items.d: Xona's precision timing and navigation service will enter beta testing after SpaceX launches six satellites designed by the company.
items.fullText: The first precision commercial alternative to GPS is preparing to go live when six satellites designed by the startup Xona Space Systems launch into orbit this month. A service that competes with free signals provided by governments around the world may seem foolhardy, but Xona is hoping to add navigation and timing to the list of de facto government space monopolies disrupted by venture-backed startups. Xona was founded in 2019 by a team of five engineers who originally met at Stanford University’s aerospace engineering graduate program. One, Tyler Reid, went on to earn a PhD, writing his thesis on the possibilities of using satellites in low-earth orbit to improve navigation. GPS and analog satellite networks built by Europe, China, and Russia provide huge value, but are also easy to jam and aren’t precise enough to be used alone for applications like farming robots or self-driving cars. Over “pizza and beer chats,” the friends mulled whether fixing those problems could be a business. “My knee jerk was like, this is dumb,” Xona CEO Brian Manning told TechCrunch during a recent visit to the company’s headquarters. “Why would anybody replace GPS? It’s free, right? And I started digging into it. People think of GPS as a free service, but the market isn’t the service. The market’s the hardware, and you have billions of devices being sold every year; those things aren’t being given away for free. There’s an immense market that is desperately looking for better performance.” That didn’t mean the road to delivering such a service was simple. Improving GPS with a stronger signal that offers more precise timing and location data remained a technical challenge. items.t: In new Elon Musk documentary, his lieutenants are the most damning voices
items.d: ‘Musk,’ the new film from Alex Gibney, features interviews with more than the usual critics of the Tesla and SpaceX CEO.
items.fullText: ANALYSIS Elon Musk Elon Musk In new Elon Musk documentary, his lieutenants are the most damning voices “Musk,” the new film from Alex Gibney, features interviews with more than the usual critics of the Tesla and SpaceX CEO. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 SpaceX CEO Elon Musk in Washington on Sept. 29. Kent Nishimura / AFP via Getty Share Add NBC News to Google Oct. 9, 2026, 5:00 AM EDT By David Ingram SAN RAFAEL, Calif. — It’s easy to find people with bad things to say about tech magnate Elon Musk, and plenty of those people show up in “Musk,” a new documentary about his rise to political and corporate power. What’s more surprising in the film are the unflattering statements by some of his own employees, including ones who still work for him. Some of the harshest scenes in the film, which opens Friday in Los Angeles and New York, are ones in which Musk’s lieutenants were recorded on video or in audio as they wielded power on his behalf or discussed what they had already done for him. Warning: This article includes spoilers for the documentary “Musk.” There are clips of Ashok Elluswamy, a high-ranking Tesla engineer, acknowledging in a videotaped deposition that an infamous hype video he helped put together in 2016 about the company’s self-driving capabilities was not an accurate representation of Tesla’s technology at the time. There are also audio snippets from Jared Birchall, who handles Musk’s personal matters. He is heard on a recording of a phone call with online influencer Ashley St. Clair, shortly after she had given birth to a child she and Musk conceived, in which he plays hardball on child support arrangements. Both incidents were documented in the media: Reuters reported in 2023 on the transcript of Elluswamy’s deposition , and The Wall Street Journal reported last year on Birchall’s phone call with St. Clair. items.d: President Donald Trump joined Michael Kratsios to award the Medal of Science to Elon Musk, Jensen Huang, Lisa Su and Sergey Brin amid announcements about new science funding.
items.fullText: Artificial intelligence Trump awards Musk and other tech titans National Medals of Science President Donald Trump joined Michael Kratsios to award the Medal of Science to Elon Musk, Jensen Huang, Lisa Su and Sergey Brin amid announcements about new science funding. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk receives the National Medal of Science from President Donald Trump at the Science: A New Golden Age Summit at the U.S. Institute of Peace on Thursday. Win McNamee / Getty Share Add NBC News to Google Oct. 8, 2026, 5:43 PM EDT By Jared Perlo WASHINGTON — President Donald Trump joined some of America’s most powerful tech leaders Thursday at a summit the White House billed as the start of a “golden age” of American science. Elon Musk, Google co-founder Sergey Brin, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, AMD CEO Lisa Su, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella and Dell founder Michael Dell gathered with Trump and a host of administration officials and scientific luminaries for the Science: A New Golden Age Summit at the U.S. Institute of Peace. “We live in an age of American wonders and technological marvels, and with the help of the brilliant men and women here today, we will always be on top,” Trump said. Trump awarded the National Medal of Science to Musk, Brin, Huang and Su. He awarded the National Medal of Technology and Innovation to Nadella and Dell. Michael Kratsios, director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, addresses the audience Thursday afternoon at the U.S. Institute of Peace. Jared Perlo / NBC News Trump presented each of the recipients with medals and certificates of honor, later asking some of their families to join him onstage to take photos. “You’re going to go down in the annals of history as being great,” Trump told the recipients.
